source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN Examination, 7th ed.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client with heart failure has magnesium 0.75 mEq/L. What should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: Normal magnesium is 1.3–2.1 mEq/L. Hypomagnesemia affects myocardial function, so the client is monitored for dysrhythmias.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q5 (PDF p. 142)
questions.quote: The client should be monitored for dysrhythmias because magnesium plays an important role in myocardial

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client with myasthenia gravis becomes WEAKER after an edrophonium (Tensilon) test dose. How is this interpreted?
questions.rationale: Worsening weakness after edrophonium means cholinergic crisis from overmedication. Improvement would mean myasthenic crisis.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q11 (PDF p. 149)
questions.quote: cholinergic crisis (overmedication) with anticholinesterase medications

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: What should the nurse do before starting continuous IV therapy?
options: Pad an arm board above the site
questions.rationale: IV solutions must be free of particles and within the expiration date to prevent vein trauma, thromboembolism, and infection.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q21 (PDF p. 160)
questions.quote: IV solutions should be free of particles or precipitates

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: What must be written on an ABG requisition?
questions.rationale: An ABG requisition includes the time drawn, the client's temperature, whether on room air or oxygen, and ventilator settings.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q31 (PDF p. 170)
questions.quote: the client’s temperature, whether the specimen was drawn on room air or using supplemental oxygen

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: What is MOST important to assess before advancing a client from liquid to solid food?
questions.rationale: Chewing ability is assessed for safety; a soft or mechanically chopped diet may be needed.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q36 (PDF p. 175)
questions.quote: The nurse needs to assess the client’s chewing ability before advancing a client from liquid to solid food.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which ABG does the nurse expect in a client on continuous NG suction?
questions.rationale: NG suction removes acid, causing metabolic alkalosis: high pH and high bicarbonate.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q40 (PDF p. 179)
questions.quote: metabolic alkalosis resulting from loss of acid

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client on NG suction has HCO3 30. Which pH is MOST likely?
questions.rationale: Loss of gastric HCl causes metabolic alkalosis, with HCO3 above normal and an elevated pH.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q73 (PDF p. 218)
questions.quote: Loss of gastric fluid via nasogastric suction or vomiting causes metabolic alkalosis

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: ABG: pH 7.43, PCO2 31, HCO3 21. Which imbalance is present?
questions.rationale: pH is normal (compensated) but on the alkaline side. Low PCO2 is the primary change, and low HCO3 is compensation.
explanations: pH is on the alkaline side.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q72 (PDF p. 217)
questions.quote: In a respiratory condition, the pH and the Pco2 move in opposite directions

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which effect should a preoperative client expect from relaxation therapy?
questions.rationale: Relaxation decreases cognitive and physiological arousal, giving a sense of well-being and lowering heart rate, BP, and muscle tension.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q42 (PDF p. 181)
questions.quote: Relaxation is the state of generalized decreased cognitive, physiological, and/or behavioral arousal.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Which Mantoux test result is POSITIVE in a client with no special risk factors?
questions.rationale: Positivity is based on induration, not redness. Under Philippine TB guidelines, induration of 10 mm or more is positive for most clients (5 mm or more if HIV-positive or immunosuppressed). A wheal only shows correct injection.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q67 (PDF p. 212)
questions.quote: The presence of a wheal would indicate that the skin test was administered appropriately.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: Where should the nurse inject a tuberculin skin test?
options: Inner forearm near a burn scar
questions.rationale: Intradermal tests are usually given on the inner forearm in an area that is not heavily pigmented and is free of lesions, scars, and hair.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q222 (PDF p. 377)
questions.quote: Intradermal injections are most commonly given in the inner surface of the forearm.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which CSF finding is normally NEGATIVE in an adult?
questions.rationale: Normal CSF has no red blood cells. Protein and glucose are normally present, and a few WBCs may be seen.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q77 (PDF p. 222)
questions.quote: The adult with a normal CSF has no red blood cells in the CSF.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which meal BEST promotes wound healing in a burn client?
questions.rationale: Wound healing needs protein (chicken, milk) and vitamin C (broccoli, strawberries).
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q78 (PDF p. 223)
questions.quote: including protein, such as chicken and milk, and vitamin C, such as broccoli and strawberries.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A client has a poor swallowing reflex. Which food should be removed from the diet?
questions.rationale: Raw, chunky, and stringy vegetables such as spinach, corn, and peas are excluded when swallowing is poor.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q80 (PDF p. 225)
questions.quote: stringy vegetables such as spinach, corn, and peas are foods commonly excluded

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: During a first walk after abdominal surgery, which sign suggests orthostatic hypotension?
questions.rationale: Orthostatic hypotension on rising causes dizziness, nausea, tachycardia, and pallor.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q83 (PDF p. 228)
questions.quote: Orthostatic hypotension occurs when a normotensive person develops symptoms of low blood pressure when rising

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: How should the client be positioned after a bedside liver biopsy?
questions.rationale: The client lies on the right side with a small pillow under the puncture site for about 2 hours to compress the liver and prevent bleeding.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q98 (PDF p. 246)
questions.quote: the nurse positions the client on the right side with a small pillow or folded towel under the puncture site

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: What is MOST important to assess before a liver biopsy?
questions.rationale: The client must lie still and hold the breath during needle insertion to avoid puncturing the lung or other organs.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q230 (PDF p. 385)
questions.quote: It is most important for the nurse to assess the client’s ability to lie still and hold the breath for the procedure.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which medication is likely prescribed before an MRI for a client with a suspected brain tumor?
questions.rationale: The client must lie still in an enclosed scanner, so relaxation techniques or a sedative may be used.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q124 (PDF p. 274)
questions.quote: An MRI scan is a noninvasive diagnostic test that visualizes the body’s tissues, structure, and blood flow.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: How should the nurse prepare a client for electrophysiology studies (EPS)?
questions.rationale: EPS is invasive and induces dysrhythmias. The client is NPO 6 to 8 hours, and antidysrhythmics are usually withheld.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q127 (PDF p. 277)
questions.quote: During this invasive procedure, a special wire is introduced into the heart to produce dysrhythmias.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: An older client with type 1 diabetes has gastroenteritis. How should the nurse prevent dehydration?
questions.rationale: Dehydration risks DKA. Small amounts of fluid are tolerated even with vomiting and are offered frequently.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q129 (PDF p. 279)
questions.quote: Small amounts of fluid may be tolerated, even when vomiting is present.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Before a kidney CT with contrast, what is MOST important to assess?
questions.rationale: Any test with possible dye requires asking about allergies, especially to iodine or shellfish.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q137 (PDF p. 287)
questions.quote: specifically an allergy to shellfish or iodine.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which condition LOWERS the risk of aspiration during enteral feeding?
questions.rationale: Sedation, coughing, artificial airways, suctioning, and decreased LOC raise aspiration risk. Head elevation reduces it.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q148 (PDF p. 298)
questions.quote: A serious complication associated with enteral feedings is aspiration of formula into the tracheobronchial tree.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: How does the nurse check for IV infiltration?
questions.rationale: Infiltration causes edema and coolness from fluid leaking into tissue. Redness and warmth suggest phlebitis.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q160 (PDF p. 311)
questions.quote: it is important to assess the site for edema and coolness

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: An IV dressing is damp and the tape is loose. What should the nurse do FIRST?
questions.rationale: The nurse checks all connections first to find the leak. If the leak is at the site, the infusion is stopped and the IV restarted.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q168 (PDF p. 321)
questions.quote: the nurse checks all connections to ensure tight seals while the IV infuses to help locate the source of the leak.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which finding suggests a need for IV fluid and electrolyte therapy?
questions.rationale: Fluid and electrolyte imbalances such as hyponatremia, with a rapid, weak, thready pulse, signal the need for IV therapy.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q172 (PDF p. 325)
questions.quote: Rapid, weak, and thready pulse is an assessment abnormality found with fluid and electrolyte imbalances, such as hyponatremia.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client with chest pain has elevated CK-MB and troponins. What do these indicate?
questions.rationale: CK-MB and troponins are sensitive markers of myocardial damage. CK-MB rises 3–6 hours after chest pain and peaks at about 24 hours.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q178 (PDF p. 331)
questions.quote: Creatine kinase (CK)-MB isoenzyme is a sensitive indicator of myocardial damage.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client needs three pillows to breathe while sleeping. How should this be documented?
questions.rationale: Orthopnea is difficulty breathing when lying flat and is documented by the number of pillows needed.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q185 (PDF p. 338)
questions.quote: Dyspnea can be exertional or at rest.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which sweat test result supports cystic fibrosis?
questions.rationale: Abnormally high sweat chloride is unique to CF; a level above 60 mEq/L supports the diagnosis.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q194 (PDF p. 348)
questions.quote: A consistent finding of abnormally high chloride concentrations in the sweat is a unique characteristic of CF.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Thoracentesis fluid has a high RBC count. What is the likely cause of the effusion?
questions.rationale: Pleural fluid with many RBCs may result from trauma and may need chest tube drainage.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q228 (PDF p. 383)
questions.quote: Pleural fluid from an effusion that has a high red blood cell count may result from trauma

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which tray should be at the bedside of a client admitted with a left pleural effusion?
questions.rationale: A significant pleural effusion is usually treated by thoracentesis, and the fluid is analyzed for the cause.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q269 (PDF p. 426)
questions.quote: The client with a significant pleural effusion is usually treated by thoracentesis.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which GI study should be scheduled LAST?
questions.rationale: Barium may take up to 72 hours to clear and can obscure other tests, so it is done last.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q229 (PDF p. 384)
questions.quote: When barium is instilled into the lower GI tract, it may take up to 72 hours to clear the GI tract.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which order does the nurse expect after an upper GI series?
questions.rationale: Barium is constipating and can cause obstruction, so laxatives are given routinely.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q316 (PDF p. 480)
questions.quote: Barium sulfate, which is used as a contrast material during an upper GI series, is constipating.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: How should the client breathe during indirect laryngoscopy?
questions.rationale: The vocal cords are observed during rest and phonation; the client sits upright and breathes normally.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q250 (PDF p. 407)
questions.quote: Indirect laryngoscopy is done to assess the function of the vocal cords or obtain tissue for biopsy.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Before a renal biopsy, which result should be reported?
questions.rationale: Hemorrhage is a main complication of renal biopsy. Normal PT is 11–12.5 seconds, so 15 seconds is prolonged.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q263 (PDF p. 420)
questions.quote: Postprocedure hemorrhage is a complication after renal biopsy.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client with pyelonephritis vomited all night and is due for an IV pyelogram. What is the PRIORITY?
questions.rationale: IV fluids replace losses, are needed for dye injection, and help eliminate the dye.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q266 (PDF p. 423)
questions.quote: The highest priority of the nurse would be to request a prescription for an intravenous infusion.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which food should a client on a low-sodium diet avoid?
questions.rationale: High-sodium foods include table salt, cheeses, soy sauce, cured pork such as ham, canned foods, and cold cuts.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q272 (PDF p. 429)
questions.quote: Foods highest in sodium include table salt, some cheeses, soy sauce, cured pork

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: What should the nurse tell a client about first cardiac catheterization?
questions.rationale: The client may feel sensations such as warmth or flushing with dye and palpitations. It is done in the cath lab under local anesthesia.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q277 (PDF p. 434)
questions.quote: Cardiac catheterization is an invasive test that involves the insertion of a catheter and the injection of dye

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client scheduled for pneumonectomy asks how long chest tubes will stay in. What should the nurse say?
questions.rationale: After pneumonectomy, chest tubes usually are not inserted; the empty cavity fills with serosanguineous fluid.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q322 (PDF p. 487)
questions.quote: Chest tubes are not inserted
